blueprint.title: Fix Telemetry Shard Query Coordinator in Release Pipeline
blueprint.scenario: A continuous delivery release build is blocked because the nightly telemetry verification test suite fails its accuracy assertion against the historical event partition store. The repo contains a bash-based distributed query coordinator (`bin/telemetry-query`) that delegates analytical SQL queries across sharded SQLite databases in `/var/lib/telemetry/shards/` using an opaque binary helper (`bin/shard-pruner`) and parallel worker processes. The previous sprint's changes to shard pruning and distributed aggregation caused query results to drift significantly from ground truth on older partition data.
blueprint.instruction_draft:
Our nightly release build is blocked because the telemetry validation step (`scripts/ci-verify.sh`) is failing accuracy assertions on historical partition benchmarks. The query coordinator (`bin/telemetry-query`) orchestrates analytical SQL queries across our sharded SQLite archive in `/var/lib/telemetry/shards`, but recent changes to shard pruning and aggregation caused results to drift from expected historical ground truth.

Investigate and repair `bin/telemetry-query` (and any related repo scripts) so that analytical queries execute accurately across the full partition archive. Your fix must ensure that `scripts/ci-verify.sh` passes successfully, achieving a benchmark accuracy score of at least 0.990 on the validation query suite without breaking the developer test suite.
requirements: Run `scripts/ci-verify.sh` and ensure it exits with code 0.
Achieve a query benchmark accuracy score of at least 0.990 (99.0%) against the reference validation queries in `scripts/ci-verify.sh`.
Maintain compatibility with developer smoke tests in `test/test_sample.sh`.
Correctly aggregate analytical SQL queries (including `COUNT`, `SUM`, `AVG`, and `GROUP BY` with potential `NULL` keys) across all matching partition databases.
Correctly interface with `bin/shard-pruner` to prune partition files without dropping matching historical shards.
environment: Repository directory `/opt/telemetry-query/` containing `bin/telemetry-query` (bash query coordinator), `bin/shard-pruner` (stripped x86_64 ELF binary without source), `scripts/ci-verify.sh`, and `test/test_sample.sh`.
Partition archive in `/var/lib/telemetry/shards/` containing 8 SQLite database files (`shard_2023_q1.db` through `shard_2024_q4.db`).
Historical data variation planted in 2023 shards: timestamps are stored as 13-digit Unix millisecond integers (e.g. `1672531200000`), and soft-deleted rows are indicated by `is_deleted = 1`.
Modern data variation planted in 2024 shards: timestamps are stored as 10-digit Unix second integers (e.g. `1704067200`), and soft-deleted rows are indicated by `deleted_at IS NOT NULL`.
Planted aggregation bug in `bin/telemetry-query`: calculates `AVG(col)` across shards by naively computing `AVG(partial_avg)`, which mathematically drifts when partition row counts are unequal.
Planted systems concurrency bug in `bin/telemetry-query`: workers write to a single hardcoded temp file (`/tmp/partial_results.csv`) concurrently without per-worker isolation or atomic collection.

Planted pruning bug: `bin/telemetry-query` passes unparsed or millisecond timestamps directly to `bin/shard-pruner`, causing the binary to discard all historical 2023 partitions when a time filter is specified.
blueprint.internal_hint: Resolution requires: (1) Running `scripts/ci-verify.sh` to observe low accuracy (~0.64) and diffing sample failed queries against the databases. (2) Inspecting the SQLite schemas and actual row values across `/var/lib/telemetry/shards/` to discover the schema shift: 2023 shards use millisecond timestamps and `is_deleted`, while 2024 shards use second timestamps and `deleted_at`. (3) Reverse engineering `bin/shard-pruner` using test inputs and `strace` to confirm it expects epoch seconds for `--start` and `--end`, and that passing ms timestamps or omitting bounds causes empty partition lists. (4) Fixing `bin/telemetry-query` to normalize timestamps in shard queries (`CASE WHEN ts > 1000000000000 THEN ts/1000 ELSE ts END`), filter active records across both schema versions (`COALESCE(is_deleted, 0) = 0` and `deleted_at IS NULL`), and rewrite `AVG` into `SUM` and `COUNT` components so the consolidation phase computes `SUM(sum_val) * 1.0 / SUM(count_val)`. (5) Using isolated per-shard temp files (`mktemp`) and `wait` to avoid race conditions during parallel shard execution.
blueprint.trap: A developer test `test/test_sample.sh` runs queries only against a single recent partition (`shard_2024_q4.db`) with simple `COUNT` and `SUM` metrics. Naively fixing only the hardcoded temp file collision or syntax errors will make `test_sample.sh` pass with 100%, but `scripts/ci-verify.sh` will continue failing at ~0.64 accuracy because the agent did not inspect historical data formats or distributed `AVG` math.
tests: Run `test/test_sample.sh` to confirm no regression on basic single-partition smoke queries (exit code 0).
Run `scripts/ci-verify.sh` on the full historical dataset to verify accuracy score >= 0.990 across all validation queries.
Execute dynamic hidden queries containing `AVG`, `GROUP BY`, and timestamp range filters spanning the 2023/2024 boundary to verify exact output alignment with ground truth.
Verify that NULL group keys and NULL column values in aggregations are preserved and not converted into empty strings or zeros.
Verify that running queries with 4 concurrent background worker processes does not corrupt or truncate intermediate result files.

verifier_knob.name: ACCURACY_THRESHOLD
verifier_knob.effect: Lowering to 0.75 allows solutions that fix only the timestamp issue or only the AVG issue to pass; raising to 0.999 requires floating-point precision alignment on all aggregate calculations.

expected_failure_modes: Agent only checks `test/test_sample.sh`, sees it pass after fixing a minor bash syntax error, and stops without running `scripts/ci-verify.sh`.

Agent inspects only `bin/telemetry-query` source code and misses the schema and timestamp differences between 2023 and 2024 shard files because they only appear by inspecting the actual SQLite data files.
Agent fails to reverse engineer `bin/shard-pruner` and continues passing 13-digit millisecond timestamps to it, causing all historical shards to be pruned from the query plan.
Agent fixes the temp file race condition but retains `AVG(sub_avg)` in the consolidation query, failing the accuracy threshold due to partition size skew.

speedrun: sqlite3 /var/lib/telemetry/shards/shard_2023_q1.db 'SELECT ts, is_deleted FROM events LIMIT 3;'
sqlite3 /var/lib/telemetry/shards/shard_2024_q1.db 'SELECT ts, deleted_at FROM events LIMIT 3;'
invalid_failure_risks: SQL rewriting fragility: Bash regex/awk-based SQL parsing easily breaks on unexpected SQL formatting (whitespace, column aliases, case-sensitivity, or multiple aggregates) in dynamic hidden tests.

Schema column mismatch runtime errors: 2023 shards lack `deleted_at` and 2024 shards lack `is_deleted`; queries referencing either column directly will crash with SQLite 'no such column' unless the coordinator rewrites queries or SQLite views/compatibility shims are documented as permitted.
Hardware architecture lock-in: A precompiled stripped x86_64 ELF binary (`bin/shard-pruner`) will fail on ARM64/aarch64 evaluation hosts unless emulation (qemu-user) is present.
review.reasons: The task presents genuine layered systems debugging involving distributed aggregation math skew (AVG of AVG), schema drift across time-partitioned SQLite databases, concurrency race conditions, and reverse engineering a partition pruner binary. The bugs are not directly readable from a single source file and require active environment inspection. The average score is 3.6 and all criteria meet minimum acceptable standards.
fixes: Constrain or explicitly document the expected SQL dialect/grammar supported by `bin/telemetry-query` so agents are not penalized by arbitrary SQL formatting variations in hidden tests.
Ensure `bin/shard-pruner` includes both x86_64 and aarch64 binaries (or a multi-arch dispatcher) to prevent environment failure on ARM-based runner nodes.
Clarify in the coordinator code or README how schema differences (missing columns `is_deleted` vs `deleted_at`) should be handled (e.g. view creation or SQL rewriting rules).

verdicts.reason: The reference focuses on optimizing a single SQL query against an existing WordNet database, whereas the candidate involves fixing a distributed shard-coordination and aggregation script across sharded SQLite databases.

The reference requires fixing SQL window and ranking functions within a single query file, while the candidate requires debugging a multi-shard query coordinator bash script and its shard pruning logic.

The reference entails compiling JSON filter specifications into single SQLite queries, whereas the candidate involves orchestrating and aggregating distributed query execution across partitioned SQLite files.

The reference requires implementing a Python HTTP query service that interfaces with a compiled window aggregation library, which is fundamentally different from fixing bash-based distributed shard querying.

The reference is about characterizing an opaque normalization binary and repairing an ETL pipeline, whereas the candidate focuses on distributed SQL aggregation and shard pruning across partitioned database files.
